## Background

This Protection Profile (PP) is developed based on Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (eIDAS 2.0), and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2981.

The architectural configuration described in this PP, hereafter referred to as the Remote HSM architecture, is one of the deployment models contemplated by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2981 for the certification of European Digital Identity Wallets. Article 2(4) of that Regulation defines the WSCA as an application that manages critical assets by being linked to and using the cryptographic and non-cryptographic functions provided by the WSCD. In the Remote HSM architecture, the WSCA executes on Wallet Provider backend infrastructure (WSCA-BE), while the WSCD is implemented as a certified remote HSM. The HSM manages the critical private keys of the Wallet Unit, including the attested keys for the KA and, if applicable, the WIA device-binding key pair. The Wallet Instance additionally holds a device-resident key in hardware-backed storage (e.g., a Secure Element or platform-provided hardware-backed keystore), which serves as the possessionbased authentication factor for remote authentication to the WSCA/WSCD.

This PP applies to the WSCA-BE as a standalone Target of Evaluation (TOE) for Common Criteria evaluation under the EUCC scheme established by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/482. A certificate of conformity issued against this PP may serve as an assurance input for national wallet certification schemes pursuant to Article 4 of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2981. The TOE of this PP will require a secure and certified WSCD as well as a secured underlying server and secure operational environment as defined by the objectives in chapter 4.

## Terminology

This Protection Profile uses the terminology defined in the European Digital Identity Wallet Architecture and Reference Framework (ARF) and the applicable EU regulations. Unless otherwise stated, terms such as Wallet Unit, Wallet Instance, Wallet Secure Cryptographic Application (WSCA), Wallet Secure Cryptographic Device (WSCD), Wallet Provider, Wallet User, Wallet Instance Attestation (WIA), Key Attestation (KA), and critical assets shall have the meaning defined in the ARF and the applicable Commission Implementing Regulations.

Where this Protection Profile introduces terms specific to the Remote HSM architecture, these terms are explicitly defined in this Protection Profile. In case of ambiguity, the definitions in the applicable EU legislation take precedence over terminology introduced in this Protection Profile. The following terms defining the secure authentication protocol between the Wallet Instance and the WSCA/WSCD are specific to the Remote HSM architecture:

- Remote User Authentication Protocol (RUAP): The protocol enforces that every PIN verification is performed through a live and fresh interaction between the Wallet Instance and the WSCA. This ensures that the confidentiality of the PIN is preserved, while verification is subject to controlled and rate limited processing at the WSCA. The Wallet Instance must demonstrate the User Authentication Evidence (UAE), which is derived both from a knowledge-based factor (derived from the PIN) and a possessionbased factor. The User Authentication Evidence (UAE) is verified against the Authentication Reference Data (ARD) which is shared during enrolment.

- Authentication Reference Data (ARD): Authentication Reference Data is shared with the WSCA/WSCD during enrolment and used at the WSCA/WSCD to verify the Authentication Reference Data (UAE).
- User Authentication Evidence (UAE) Cryptographic evidence bound to a user authentication event at the wallet instance, provided over the Remote Authentication Channel and verified by the WSCA before it performs a wallet cryptographic operation.

## Relationship to Other Standards and Schemes

This Protection Profile is intended to be used within the legal, regulatory, certification and technical framework established by the following documents and standards.

- eIDAS 2.0: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183, establishing the European Digital Identity Framework.
- EUDI Wallet Certification: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2981, laying down rules for the certification of European Digital Identity Wallets.
- EUCC Scheme: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/482 establishing the European Common Criteria-based cybersecurity certification scheme (EUCC), including its applicable amendments and supporting documents.
- EUDI Wallet Core Functionality and Integrity: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2979.
- EUDI Wallet Protocols and Interfaces: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2982.
- PID and EAA: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2977, laying down rules concerning person identification data and electronic attestations of attributes.
- Applicable Standards and Specifications: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1731, amending Regulations (EU) 2024/2977, 2024/2979, 2024/2980 and 2024/2982 with updated standards and specifications.
- Wallet-Relying Parties: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/848 concerning the registration of wallet-relying parties and their access certificates.
- Certified Wallets: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/849 concerning the submission of information to the Commission and the Cooperation Group for the list of certified EUDI Wallets.
- Assurance Levels for Electronic Identification: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502.
- EUDI Wallet Architecture and Reference Framework (ARF): The current applicable version of the ARF, including its requirements, definitions, technical specifications, rulebooks and certification requirements. The ARF provides the technical architecture and reference specifications supporting the EUDI Wallet ecosystem.
- ECCG Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms (ACM): The current applicable version.
- Common Criteria: Latest version published on the CCRA publications page, as applicable through the EUCC scheme.
- Cryptographic and PKI standards: Applicable ETSI, ISO/IEC and IETF standards referenced by the ARF and the applicable implementing regulations.
- CEN Protection Profile for TSP Cryptographic Modules: EN 419 221-5:2018, Protection Profiles for TSP Cryptographic Modules – Part 5: Cryptographic Module for Trust Services. Applicable to the cryptographic functionality and key protection provided by the WSCD; the WSCD may claim conformance to this Protection Profile.

### 1.2 TOE Overview {#s-1-2}

The Target of Evaluation (TOE) is the Wallet Secure Cryptographic Application (WSCA) deployed in the wallet provider’s back-end infrastructure (WSCA-BE (TOE)). The TOE operates as an authenticated remote signing service: it verifies the user’s identity and authorisation, validates the wallet instance key binding, and instructs the Wallet Secure Cryptographic Device (WSCD-HSM) to generate signing keys and to sign the data submitted by the Wallet Instance used in the communication with the PID/Attestation providers and the relying parties. The TOE manages the full lifecycle of Attested key pairs (and optionally WIA device-binding key pairs). However, the attested private keys will never leave the security context of the WSCD-HSM. All cryptographic operations are handled by the WSCD-HSM, which resides in the WSCA-BE physical protected environment.

#### 1.2.1 The Wallet Instance (TOE) in the Wallet Ecosystem {#s-1-2-1}

The Wallet Secure Cryptographic Application deployed in the backend, WSCA-BE, is one of the components in the Wallet Unit, which acts as part of the Wallet Ecosystem. In Figure 1, the main components of the Wallet Unit and Wallet Ecosystem are depicted.

Figure 1 — The wallet Unit in the Wallet Ecosystem

![Image](/img/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/nl-cs-wsca/image_000000_46657bcb06cee2feb92c9eb59a5e3c5ba406cdf74207505e8c62115b6d38b2f1.png)

#### 1.2.2 Wallet Unit components {#s-1-2-2}

The following components are the core components in the Wallet Unit, as depicted in Figure 1:

User device (UD): The hardware, operating system and software environment on which the Wallet Instance executes. The User Device provides the execution environment, local security mechanisms and a local key store for the Wallet Instance. The local key store may be used to generate, store and use critical cryptographic assets. The security posture of the User Device, including the integrity of its operating system and relevant security mechanisms, contributes to the overall security of the Wallet Unit.

- Wallet Instance (WI): The mobile application installed on the User Device. The Wallet Instance authenticates ecosystem entities, obtains User approval for securitysensitive actions, manages credentials and cryptographic assets, and initiates cryptographic operations. It shall protect sensitive Wallet User information and ensure that security-sensitive operations are performed only under the applicable authorization and User-control conditions. It interfaces with a local key store on the user device for the management of critical cryptographic assets.
- Wallet Secure Cryptographic Application (WSCA-BE) (TOE): A WSCA-BE implementation deployed on a hardened backend server. It provides security-critical cryptographic functionality sourced through interfaces with the WSCD. The WSCA-BE enforces the applicable security controls for cryptographic operations and ensures that operations involving critical assets are performed only after the required authorization and User authentication conditions have been satisfied.
- Wallet Secure Cryptographic Device (WSCD): A hardware security device used by the WSCA to protect critical cryptographic assets and perform security-sensitive cryptographic operations. The WSCD shall protect the confidentiality and integrity of protected private keys and shall prevent unauthorized export or use of protected private keys. The WSCD shall be certified against a cryptographic module certified protection profile EN 419 221-5:2018 or a different applicable Protection Profile providing at least equivalent functionality and assurance.

#### 1.2.3 Wallet Ecosystem Entities {#s-1-2-3}

The following entities (depicted in Figure 1) are part of the Wallet Ecosystem and interact with the Wallet Unit:

- Wallet Provider Backend (WPB): Provides Wallet Provider services, including Wallet Unit onboarding, activation, management, maintenance and security-status related services. The Wallet Provider is responsible for establishing the required trust relationship with the Wallet Instance, issuing the WIA and KA, and taking appropriate action when the security or trustworthiness of a Wallet Unit is compromised.
- PID and Attestation Providers: Providers that issue PIDs and Attestations to the Wallet Unit. Before issuance, the Provider authenticates the Wallet Unit and verifies the applicable WIA and KA, including their validity and revocation status. For device-bound credentials, the Provider verifies proof-of-possession of the private key corresponding to the public key contained in the KA and binds the issued credential to that key.
- Relying Parties (RPs): Entities that request and verify PID or Attestation attributes from the Wallet Unit to provide a service to the User. The RP authenticates to the Wallet Unit using the applicable Access Certificate and provides the information required for the User to understand and approve the requested disclosure. The RP is responsible for verifying the authenticity, integrity, freshness and applicable cryptographic binding of the received presentation.
- Access Certificate Infrastructure: (not in in Figure 1): Provides Access Certificates used to authenticate relevant ecosystem entities. The associated trust infrastructure provides the trust anchors required by the Wallet Unit and other ecosystem participants to verify the authenticity of Access Certificates.

#### 1.2.4 Principal security interactions {#s-1-2-4}

The principal high level data flows and trust relationships are as follows between the entities:

- WSCA-BE (TOE) — Wallet Instance (WI): The Wallet Instance communicates with the WSCA-BE (TOE) through a mutually authenticated and protected channel providing confidentiality and integrity. User Authentication and the Remote User Authentication Protocol (RUAP), including User Authentication Evidence (UAE) and Authentication Reference Data (ARD), are used to authenticate the User and authorise security-sensitive operations. The WSCA invokes the WSCD for operations involving protected cryptographic assets.
- WSCA-BE (TOE) — WSCD: The WSCA-BE communicates with the WSCD using the secure channel supported by the WSCD. Per-key authentication shall be implemented to ensure that security-sensitive cryptographic operations are authorised before execution by the WSCD. Per-key authentication data shall be securely deleted from the TOE and be managed by the WI and provided the TOE as required for the requested operation.
- WSCA-BE (TOE) — Wallet Provider Backend (WPB): The WSCA-BE provides an authentication mechanisms required for the Wallet Provider to authenticate the attested public keys before using them to issue and sign the Key Attestation (KA) and Wallet Instance Attestation (WIA).

All communication between the WSCA-BE and the WPB shall be conducted over a secure channel providing mutual authentication, confidentiality and integrity.

- Wallet Instance — Wallet Provider Backend (WPB): The Wallet Instance communicates with the Wallet Provider for installation, onboarding, activation, Wallet Unit management and security-status-related services. During onboarding and activation, the Wallet Provider receives the attested keys and, where applicable, the

WIA device-binding key material, and securely provides the WIA and KA to the Wallet Instance.

- Wallet Instance — PID/Attestation Providers: The Wallet Instance communicates with PID and Attestation Providers to request and receive PIDs or Attestations. Where required, the Wallet Unit provides the applicable WIA and KA. The Provider verifies these objects and may request proof of possession of the corresponding private keys before issuing a device-bound credential. The WSCA/WSCD performs the required cryptographic operations and proof-of-possession using the protected private keys.
- Wallet Instance — Relying Party: The Wallet Instance participates in credential presentation using the applicable presentation protocol. It authenticates the Relying Party, evaluates the presentation request, obtains explicit User approval and performs selective disclosure. For device-bound credentials, the Wallet Unit uses the applicable WSCA/WSCD to perform the required cryptographic operations and proof-ofpossession.

#### 1.2.5 The WSCA-BE (TOE) located inside a Secure Environment {#s-1-2-5}

The WSCA-BE (TOE) is deployed on a dedicated hardened server that runs no services other than the WSBA-BE. This server is positioned behind gateway servers that manages and filters all external communications to the Wallet Provider backend and the Wallet Instance. This architecture enables the TOE to maintain a minimal and secure design. The WSCA is expected to use an external database to securely store the Authentication Reference Data (ARD) for the individual Wallet Units. Every security-relevant action is an audit log entry, which is cryptographically tied to specific wallet units and transactions, and is transmitted to an external log server.

Figure 2 — TOE deployment boundary

![Image](/img/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/nl-cs-wsca/image_000001_8bd6782b070b9194f28867d376fc4c7238537acc96f2720e7199dbecdafce5ea.png)

The WSCA-BE (TOE), the hardened server, the WSCD, the Gateway server and external databases, the log servers, and their connections, shall operate in a protected environment that limits physical access to the TOE to authorised privileged users.

##### 1.2.5.1 Non-TOE Hardware/Software {#s-1-2-5-1}

Following Figure 2, the following non-TOE Hardware and/or Software would be required:

- WSCD-HSM: An appropriate HSM following CEN EN PP 419 221-5 or a different applicable Protection Profile providing at least equivalent functionality and assurance.
- Hardened Server: The TOE underlying hardware is be hardened against remote sidechannel attacks and microarchitectural attacks.
- Gateway Server: Internet facing gateways shall be used for, at least, DDoS protection, intrusion detection, antivirus functionality and firewall functionality.
- Database: External databases used for storage of TOE assets.
- Log Server: Receives audit log messages from the TOE. The environment shall ensure that log data is not deleted.
- Wallet Provider Backend: The Wallet Provider Backend enables the Wallet Provider to connect to the TOE
- Wallet Instance: The Wallet User uses the wallet instance to request operations from the TOE. The wallet instance shall be certified according to (EU) 2024/2981.
- Reliable Time Source: A reliable time source needs to be provided to the TOE.

#### 1.2.6 The WSCA-BE (TOE) major security features {#s-1-2-6}

The WSCA-BE (TOE) has the following major security features, as it:

- Secure communication: Establishes protected communication channels between the Wallet Instance and the WSCA-BE providing mutual authentication, confidentiality and integrity, including protection against replay and message manipulation where required.
- Remote User Authentication: Implements the Remote User Authentication Protocol (RUAP), including enrolment and management of Authentication Reference Data (ARD), and verifies transaction-bound and freshly derived User Authentication Evidence (UAE) before allowing security-sensitive operations, providing sole control to user specific assets. TOE allows for PIN reset using a PUK mechanism. Per-key authentication data shall be held by the Wallet Instance and be provided at every security-sensitive cryptographic operation of the applicable key, to ensure sole control of the Wallet User before the execution by the WSCD.
- Wallet Provider authentication and authorization: Authenticates the Wallet Provider and enforces role-based access control so that Wallet Provider functions (e.g. audit data review) and security-sensitive operations can only be performed by an authenticated and authorized Wallet Provider.
- Cryptographic key management: Manages the lifecycle and metadata of Wallet Unit cryptographic keys, including attested keys and, where applicable, the WIA devicebinding key, while delegating private-key protection and cryptographic operations to the WSCD-HSM.
- WSCD-HSM access-control protection: Protects the access-control data and authorization information used to control access to WSCD-HSM services, preventing unauthorized modification or use of this data to obtain unauthorized cryptographic operations.
- Attestation support: Supports the Wallet Provider in generating and signing the Key Attestation (KA) and Wallet Instance Attestation (WIA). The TOE provides cryptographic evidence binding the attested public keys to keys generated and managed by the WSCA/WSCD, enabling the Wallet Provider to verify the authenticity of the public keys before including them in the KA or WIA.
- Protected cryptographic operations: Ensures that security-sensitive operations involving protected Wallet Unit assets are performed only following the required User authentication and authorization, while private keys remain under WSCD-HSM protection.

- Multi-tenant isolation: Provides isolation between concurrently served Wallet Units, protecting their key metadata, credentials and security-relevant data within the WSCABE and maintaining separation between tenants.
- Security audit: Generates tamper-evident audit records for security-relevant operations, attributable to the relevant Wallet Unit and transaction, and securely transfers them to the external log server.
- Self protection: Self testing, secure initalization and preserving of a secure WSCA state is mandated.

The WSCA-BE (TOE) does NOT include the WSCD-HSM hardware or firmware, the Wallet Instance application or device, log server, the Internet-facing gateway or load balancer or any wallet provider backend services other than the WSCA-BE module itself.

### 1.3 Wallet Unit Lifecycle and Cryptographic Trust Relationships {#s-1-3}

Note: This section and its subsections are of informative nature, describing the TOE and its place in EUDI Wallet ecosystem. The ST author is not expected to reproduce this section in the ST.

The WSCA-BE (TOE) forms part of a Wallet Unit within the EUDI Wallet ecosystem. This section provides context for the security and trust relationships established during the Wallet Unit lifecycle.

It describes how the WSCA-BE (TOE) interacts with the Wallet Provider, Wallet Instance, keystores, PID and Attestation Providers, and Relying Parties, and how cryptographic mechanisms are used to establish authenticity, integrity, confidentiality and cryptographic binding where required.

The section distinguishes between trust established through cryptographic mechanisms and trust established through certification, registration, trusted lists and other ecosystem governance mechanisms.

#### 1.3.1 Wallet Instance Installation {#s-1-3-1}

The Wallet Instance should preferably be distributed through an official application distribution channel of the User Device operating system. If the Wallet Instance is distributed through another mechanism, the Wallet Provider shall provide a mechanism enabling the User to verify the authenticity and integrity of the Wallet Instance before installation.

##### 1.3.1.1 Mutual Authentication Channel {#s-1-3-1-1}

After installation, the Wallet Instance establishes the required secure communication channels with:

- the Wallet Provider; and
- the WSCA/WSCD.

Communication between the Wallet Instance and Wallet Provider shall provide mutual authentication and shall provide confidentiality and integrity protection where required.

##### 1.3.1.2 Initial Data Requested by Wallet Provider {#s-1-3-1-2}

The Wallet Instance will now send its initial data to the Wallet Provider which contains technical data from the Wallet Instance, including cryptographic and hardware capabilities (such as WSCD and keystore details), system diagnostics (including OS, SDK, and library versions, plus information about available communication interfaces such as BLE and NFC), and security posture signals such as rooting, emulator, and malware detection.

The Wallet Provider shall limit collected device and security-posture information to the data necessary for Wallet Solution deployment, maintenance and security-posture monitoring. Collection shall be minimised and performed with appropriate privacy safeguards.

#### 1.3.2 Wallet Activation {#s-1-3-2}

For Wallet Activation, the following steps are performed:

- Creation of a Wallet Provider user account and association of the Wallet Instance with that account (further detailed in section 1.3.2.1).
- Registration of the User authentication methods that will be used to access and operate the wallet (further detailed in section 1.3.2.2).
- Initial Generation and issuance of the WIA and KA (further detailed in section 1.3.2.3)

During activation, the Wallet Provider establishes the required trust relationship with the Wallet Instance and provides the WIA and KA required for subsequent Wallet Unit operations. The WIA provides information about the Wallet Instance and Wallet Solution, while the KA provides information about the WSCA/WSCD or applicable keystore and the public keys used by the Wallet Unit.

The User authentication mechanisms established during activation are subsequently used to control access to the Wallet Unit and, where applicable, to protect security-sensitive cryptographic operations involving critical Wallet Unit assets.

The following sections describe the individual activation steps and the associated cryptographic assets.

##### 1.3.2.1 Wallet Provider User account {#s-1-3-2-1}

The User must register with the Wallet Provider to create a Wallet Provider User account. The wallet provider must associate the Wallet Provider User account with the installed Wallet Instance.

The Wallet Provider associates the Wallet Unit with a User account to support Wallet Unit management, including User-requested revocation. The account does not necessarily need to contain the User's real-world identity unless required for a specific Wallet function or legal obligation.

##### 1.3.2.2 User Authentications {#s-1-3-2-2}

The User enrols two user authentication mechanisms to the Wallet Instance. These two User authentication mechanisms are:

## OS-level User authentication:

- The Wallet Instance shall require OS-level User authentication whenever the Wallet Instance is opened and before performing Wallet Unit operations. The OS-level authentication mechanism shall use possession of the User Device together with a knowledge-based or inherence-based factor.
- This local OS-based authentication shall be enforced at startup of the Wallet Instance and before security-sensitive actions, such as
    - generating and presenting pseudonyms,
    - accessing the transaction log via the dashboard,
    - requesting the erasure of personal data by a Relying Party;
    - other operations as specified by the applicable ARF requirements.

WSCA/WSCD-level Remote User Authentication Protocol (RUAP):

- This specific Remote User Authentication Protocol (RUAP), including the use of User Authentication Evidence (UAE) and Authentication Reference Data (ARD), is a PP-specific mechanism defined to implement the required WSCA/WSCD-level User authentication.
- The RUAP shall support User authentication meeting the applicable requirements for Level of Assurance High as specified in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502. In particular, the authentication mechanism shall use at least two authentication factors from different categories and shall implement security controls such that guessing, eavesdropping, replay and manipulation of the authentication communication cannot, with high attack potential, subvert the authentication mechanism.
- The Wallet Instance must demonstrate the User Authentication Evidence (UAE), which is derived both from a knowledge-based authentication factor (derived from the PIN) and a possession-based authentication factor, which are jointly validated to achieve two-factor authentication and to prevent manipulation or forged attempts.
- Remote User Authentication Protocol (RUAP) ensure PIN Verification and ensure that the User has sole control over the critical assets located in the WSCD, such that these assets cannot be used without the User's involvement through the required authentication factors;
- The protocol protects the confidentiality and integrity of the authentication data during PIN verification and enrolment, and provides protection against duplication, tampering, eavesdropping and replay attacks, including through freshness and challenge binding;
- Each PIN verification is performed through a live and fresh interaction between the Wallet Instance and the WSCA/WSCD, preventing reuse of previously exchanged authentication information;
- During enrolment, the Wallet Instance Wallet Instance ensures that both the knowledge and possession factors are securely initialized and cryptographically bound to the Authentication Reference Data (ARD). Authentication Reference Data (ARD) is derived and is shared with the WSCA /WSCD during initial enrolment. This binding preserves confidentiality and integrity of the knowledge-based authentication factor (derived from the PIN) and a possession-based authentication factor and prevents compromise also if the confidentiality of the Authentication Reference Data (ARD) is not preserved.
- A Personal Unblocking Key (PUK) can be integrated in the protocol to reset the knowledge-based factor in case the PIN was forgotten.
- Per-key authentication data shall be held by the Wallet Instance and be provided at every security-sensitive cryptographic operation of the applicable key, to ensure sole control of the Wallet User before the execution by the WSCD.
- This authentication mechanism is subsequently required whenever the Wallet Unit performs cryptographic operations involving protected assets within the WSCA/WSCD, ensuring that all such operations remain securely bound to both the user and the user device. At a minimum, in the following situations. WSCA/WSCD-level User Authentication is required:
    - Initial Generation of KAs and WIA (further detailed in section 1.3.2.3).
    - The Wallet Unit asks the User for approval of selective disclosure to a Relying Party (further detailed in section 1.3.4.2)
    - The User deletes a PID or attestation and the attested keys in their Wallet Unit (further detailed in section 1.3.5).
    - The User instructs the Wallet to request the issuance of a new PID or Attestation.

##### 1.3.2.3 Initial Generation of the WIA and KA {#s-1-3-2-3}

During Wallet Activation, at least one set of Wallet Unit Attestations (WUA) is issued. These attestations comprise the Key Attestation(s) (KA) and the Wallet Instance Attestation (WIA).

The KA provides information about the WSCA/WSCD and contains the cryptographic public keys of the attested key pairs. The corresponding private keys are protected by the WSCA/WSCD. The WIA provides information about the Wallet Instance and Wallet Solution, including applicable certification information. The WIA device-binding key pair may optionally be generated within the WSCA/WSCD or managed within the context of the Wallet Instance.

The WIA and KA are issued and signed by the Wallet Provider. The WSCA/WSCD shall provide cryptographic means (signing) for the Wallet Provider to authenticate the public keys before including them in the WIA or KA.

###### 1.3.2.3.1 Key attestations (KA) {#s-1-3-2-3-1}

The User must perform WSCA/WSCD-level user authentication through the Wallet Instance to request the WSCA/WSCD to generate the attested keys for the Key Attestation (KA). The Key Attestation (KA) is a signed information object, generated and signed using the Wallet Provider signing key (WP\_SIG\_PRIV1), and contains:

- One or more attested public keys (PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEYs)
- Applicable certification and security information concerning the WSCA/WSCD.

The attested public keys (PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEYs) shall be signed by the WSCA/WSCD signing keys (WSCA/D\_PRIV\_KEY) allowing the Wallet Provider to authenticate the public keys before KA issuance.

Key Attestation (KA) has the following purposes:

- The Wallet Unit shares the KA with the PID and Attestation Providers during issuance of a device-bound PID or Attestation.
- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider verify the signature using the WP\_SIG\_PUB1, verified through a certificate chain, where the Provider’s certificate is validated through the Access Certificate Authority (ACA) up to a trusted anchor provisioned by the relevant EUDI Wallet trust framework.
- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider will use the Applicable certification and security information of the WSCA/WSCD, to verify if the WSCA/WSCD is fit to protect the private keys for a PID or Attestation or whether it is revoked.
- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider can request a proof-of-possession, by sending a nonce via the wallet instance to the WSCA/WSCD to be signed with private keys (PID/ATT\_PRIV\_KEYs) corresponding to PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEYs. This proves that the (PID/ATT\_PRIV\_KEYs) corresponding to PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEYs are generated by and stored in the WSCA/WSCD.
- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider will include the PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEYs the issued PID or Attestation.

###### 1.3.2.3.2 Wallet Instance Attestation (WIA) {#s-1-3-2-3-2}

The Wallet Instance Attestation (WIA) is a signed information object, signed by the Wallet Provider Key (WP\_SIG\_PRIV2) and contains:

- Wallet Information: Wallet Solution ID/Name, version and URIs with Certification information and additional Wallet Solution information.
- Expiration and revocation status. The technical validity period of a WIA shall be less than 24 hours.
- WIA public key: WIA\_KEY\_PUB.

The WIA device-binding key pair (WIA\_KEY\_PRIV and WIA\_KEY\_PUB) may be managed either by the WSCA/WSCD or by the Wallet Instance.

The WIA device-binding public key (WIA\_KEY\_PUB) shall be signed by the WSCA/WSCD signing keys (WSCA/D\_PRIV\_KEY) allowing the Wallet Provider to authenticate the public keys before WIA issuance.

Key Attestation has the following purposes:

- The Wallet Unit shared Wallet Instance Attestation (WIA) with the PID and Attestation Providers.
- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider verify the signature using the WP\_SIG\_PUB2, verified through a certificate chain, where the Provider’s certificate is validated through the Access Certificate Authority (ACA) up to a trusted anchor provisioned by the relevant EUDI Wallet trust framework.
- Sent to PID and Attestation Providers to inform them about the Wallet Instance details, such as Wallet Solution name, version, and certification of the Wallet Solution, and revocation status.
- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider will use the Wallet Identifiers to verify if the Wallet Unit belongs to a certified Wallet Solution registered in the Wallet Provider Trusted List.
- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider uses the revocation reference allowing a PID Provider or an Attestation Provider to verify if the Wallet Solution has been revoked.
- PID Provider or an Attestation Provider can request a proof-of-possession, by sending a nonce via the wallet instance to the WSCA/WSCD to be signed with private keys (WIA\_KEY\_PRIV) corresponding to WIA\_KEY\_PUB. This proves that the (WIA\_KEY\_PRIV) corresponding to WIA\_KEY\_PUB is managed by the Wallet Unit.

#### 1.3.3 PID/Attestation Provider authentication and Issuance. {#s-1-3-3}

Before the PID/Attestation Provider issues the PID or the Attestation to the Wallet Unit, they will first authenticate to each other.

##### 1.3.3.1 PID/Attestation Provider authentication to the Wallet Unit {#s-1-3-3-1}

The first step in the issuance process is the authentication of the Provider by the Wallet Instance.

During Provider authentication the Wallet Instance executes the following steps:

- Wallet Instance initiates connection with the PID/Attestation Provider.
- The Provider returns to the Wallet Instance its Access Certificate (ISS\_ACC\_CERT) and, where applicable, a Registration Certificate (ISS\_REG\_CERT).
- The Wallet Instance verifies the certificates using the applicable certificate chain and trusted anchor.
- The Wallet Instance verifies the Provider's registered identity, role and, where applicable, the credential types or services for which the Provider is registered. This information is obtained from the Registration Certificate or the applicable Registrar service.

##### 1.3.3.2 Wallet Unit authentication to the PID/Attestation Provider {#s-1-3-3-2}

The next step in the Issuance process is for the Wallet Instance to send the PID/attestation request (OpenID4VCI -Credential Request) to the Provider, and for the Provider to authenticate the WUAs (KA & WIA).

During WIA authentication the following steps are executed:

- Wallet Instance sends the signed WIA to the Provider.

- The Provider verifies the WIA signature using the applicable Wallet Provider public key (WP\_SIG\_PUB2). Trust in the Provider's public key shall be established through the applicable Trust List or LoTE.
- The Provider verifies the validity and revocation status of the WIA.
- The Provider requests proof-of-possession from the Wallet Unit of WIA\_KEY\_PRIV corresponding to WIA\_KEY\_PUB contained in the WIA. The Provider provides a nonce to the Wallet Instance. The Wallet Instance signs the nonce using WIA\_KEY\_PRIV, either directly or through the WSCA/WSCD where the key is stored there. The signed nonce is returned to the Provider and verified using WIA\_KEY\_PUB.

During KAs authentication the following steps are executed:

- Wallet Instance sends a signed KA(s) to the Provider.
- The Provider verifies the signatures using the Wallet Provider public (WP\_SIG\_PUB1) key. Trust in the Provider's public key shall be established through the applicable Trust List or LoTE.
- The Provider verifies the validity and revocation status of the KA.
- The Provider requires proof-of-possession from the wallet unit, of the private counterpart (PID/ATT\_PRIV\_KEY) of the public key in the KA (PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEYs), as defined in OpenID4VCI. For this, the Provider provides a nonce to the Wallet Instance. The Wallet Instance will request the WSCA/WSCD to sign this nonce with the PID/ATT\_PRIV\_KEY. The signed nonce is returned to the Provider and the Provider will verify the signature with PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEY from the KAs.
- To avoid a second request from the Wallet Instance to the WSCA/WSCD, If the Wallet Instance generates a new KA during PID/Attestation issuance the nonce can be included in the KA, and the KA is additionally signed by the PID/ATT\_PRIV\_KEYs matching the public keys in the KA (PID/ATT\_PUB\_KEYs).

The Wallet Instance sends a KA to a PID Provider or Attestation Provider only for devicebound, not for non-device-bound PIDs/Attestations.

##### 1.3.3.3 PID/Attestation Generation {#s-1-3-3-3}

Now that the Provider has ensured that it is interacting with the Wallet Unit holding the private key corresponding to the public key embedded in the KA, has verified the applicable WSCA/WSCD or keystore security properties, and has verified the Wallet Instance through the WIA, it can generate the PID or Attestation.

For a device-bound PID or Attestation, the Provider binds the issued credential to one of the public keys contained in the applicable KA. The issued PID/Attestation is signed using the Provider's private signing key (ISS\_SIG\_PRIV) and is sent to the Wallet Instance using the OpenID4VCI Credential Response.

The exact cryptographic structure of the issued PID or Attestation depends on the credential format and the applicable technical specification.

The Wallet Unit supports, where applicable:

- SD-JWT VC for remote presentation to Relying Parties.
- ISO/IEC 18013-5 mdoc for proximity presentation.

Both formats support selective disclosure based on a common high-level cryptographic principle: the credential contains cryptographic commitments, typically in the form of salted hashes, that allow individual attributes to be disclosed and subsequently verified without disclosing the other attributes. The disclosed attribute and the corresponding cryptographic information allow the Relying Party to verify that the attribute was included in the credential and protected by the Provider's signature.

The detailed cryptographic structures and verification mechanisms are format-specific and are defined by the applicable SD-JWT VC and ISO/IEC 18013-5 specifications.

For device-bound credentials, the public key associated with the protected private key is included or referenced in the credential in accordance with the applicable credential format. During presentation, the Wallet Unit uses the corresponding private key to provide the required proof of possession or device binding.

#### 1.3.4 Credential (PIDs/Attestation) Disclosure {#s-1-3-4}

At this point in the lifecycle, the Wallet Instance holds PIDs or Attestations and is ready to disclose selected attributes/claims to the Relying Party.

PIDs/Attestation selective disclosure includes the following steps:

- The Wallet Instance authenticates the Relying Party.
- The Wallet Instance requests User approval of the attributes/claims to be disclosed and performs selective disclosure.

##### 1.3.4.1 Wallet Instance authenticates Relying Party {#s-1-3-4-1}

The Wallet Instance authenticates the Relying Party using an Access Certificate (RP\_ACC\_CERT) and obtains or verifies the applicable Relying Party registration information using a Registration Certificate (RP\_REG\_CERT) or the applicable Registrar's online service.

Trust in the Access Certificate and Registration Certificate is established using the applicable trusted anchors.

The Access Certificate is used to authenticate the Relying Party or intermediary participating in the presentation transaction. The Registration Certificate or Registrar service provides information about the Relying Party's registered role, Service, intended use and applicable information relevant to the presentation request.

The Wallet Instance must inform the User of the outcome of the Relying Party authentication and certificate validation.

##### 1.3.4.2 User approval and selective disclosure {#s-1-3-4-2}

Prior to User approval, the Wallet Instance shall authenticate the User using OS-level or WSCD/WSCA-based authentication.

The Wallet Instance shall present the following information to the User and obtain explicit approval before disclosure:

- The identity of the Relying Party, and intermediary parties if present.
- Attributes/claims the Relying Party requested
- Relying Party's intended use (from Registration cert or service), and privacy policy for these attributes,
- Outcome of the evaluation of the requested attributes

The Wallet Instance shall support selective disclosure using the mechanism defined by the applicable PID/Attestation format. At a high level, the individual attributes are represented by salted cryptographic hashes that are protected by the Provider's signature. When an attribute is disclosed, the Relying Party can use the disclosed attribute and the corresponding hash information to verify that it was included in the credential, without requiring disclosure of the other attributes.

The Wallet Instance shall generate a presentation bound to the transaction, including the freshness value provided by the Relying Party, and use the WSCD/WSCA to sign the presentation with the corresponding PID/Attestation private key (PID/ATT\_PRIV\_KEY). This provides proof-of-possession of the private key.

The Relying Party shall verify the presentation, including its authenticity, integrity, freshness and the authenticity of the Provider, using the applicable credential and presentation specifications. Trust in the Provider's public key shall be established through the applicable Trust List or LoTE.

After the transaction, the Wallet Instance shall enable the User to report unlawful or suspicious requests for personal data and to request deletion of personal data from the Relying Party.

#### 1.3.5 Migration to a new Wallet Instance {#s-1-3-5}

The Wallet Unit supports secure migration of Wallet Unit contents to a new Wallet Instance. The migration process uses a protected Migration Object containing the information required to restore or re-issue applicable credentials while excluding sensitive information such as WIA, KA and private keys.

#### 1.3.6 Revocation/Deletion {#s-1-3-6}

The Wallet Provider must revoke the Wallet Unit upon explicit User request, upon an explicit request from a PID Provider in accordance with the applicable revocation procedure, and when a security breach or compromise affects the trustworthiness or reliability of the Wallet Unit.

A Wallet Instance is revoked by setting the revoked status at all index positions specified in the WIAs issued to that Wallet Instance. A WSCD is revoked by setting the revoked status at all index positions specified in the corresponding KAs.

The Wallet Unit shall support secure deletion of its contents. This shall delete all attestations, logs, personal data, settings and configurations and, where connected, request the associated WSCA/WSCD and keystores to delete the cryptographic assets related to the Wallet Unit. •
