### 3.2 Subjects {#s-3-2}

Table 2 defines the subjects that interact with the WSCA-BE.

Table 2 — Subjects

| Subjects         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| S.WalletProvider | Wallet provider backed application that communicates with the TOE through a mutually authenticated channel. This subject requests operations on the TOE.                                                                                                                                                             |
| S.WalletInstance | Wallet application that communicates with the TOE over a local or external interface. This subject requests operations on the TOE.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| S.WalletUser     | An end user of the TOE which is required to be authenticated before any cryptographic action can be carried out with the users’ keys. The S.WalletUser does not manage or use keys directly. All communication with the TOE is mediated by the S.WalletInstance. Each S.WalletUser has exactly one S.WalletInstance. |

### 3.3 Threats {#s-3-3}

This section of the security problem definition shows the threats that are to be countered by the TOE. A threat consists of a threat agent, an asset and an adverse action of that threat agent on that asset.

The threats identified against the TOE and its assets are defined in Table 3. All threats assume HIGH attack potential against the WSCA-BE, consistent with EAL4 augmented with AVA\_VAN.5 and the requirements of (EU) 2024/2981.

Table 3 — Threats

| Treat ID                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| T.WSCA_FW_TAMPER          | An attacker who compromises the TOE — through a software vulnerability, insider threat, or supply chain attack — attempts to invoke WSCD-HSM signing operations with the AST.Attested_Key_Pairs, AST.WIA_Device_binding_Key_Pair and AST.WSCA_WSCD_ Signing_Key_Pair on behalf of a victim wallet user without that user’s knowledge or consent.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| T.WSCA_ATTESTATION_TAMPER | An attacker tampers with the attestation process by submitting for signing with AST.WSCA_WSCD_Signing_Key_Pair a public key that was not generated within the WSCD-HSM for the authenticated wallet user, so that the Wallet Provider includes an attacker-controlled key in a Key Attestation or Wallet Instance Attestation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| T.WSCA_DATA_TAMPER        | An attacker modifies the AST.WSCA_BE_Software_And_Configuration_Data through server-side exploitation — such as privilege escalation, supply chain compromise, or insider threat — resulting in subversion of access controls, suppression of audit events or unauthorised access to AST.WSCD_HSM_Access_Credentials.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| T.WSCA_NET_ATTACK         | A network adversary performs active attacks (e.g. read, change, forge or replay) against the secure channel between the Wallet Instance and the WSCA-BE. This includes compromising either, AST.Channel_Authentication_Key_Pair, AST.Channel_Authentication_Session_ Key or AST.Wallet_Instance_Authentication_Data used for mutually authenticating the secure channel.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| T.REMOTE_AUTH_VUL         | An attacker exploits a vulnerability in the Remote User Authentication protocol (RUAP)— such as a forged User Authentication Evidence (UAE), or a broken session binding — to trigger a signing operation from the WSCA-BE using AST.Attested_Key_Pairs, AST.WIA_Device_binding_Key_Pair and AST.WSCA_WSCD_ Signing_Key_Pair without the legitimate wallet user’s consent. Possible RUAP attacks to be considered need to include at least guessing, eavesdropping, replay, manipulation of the authentication communication or bruteforcing the PIN (or PUK). |
| T.WALLET_ORACLE           | An attacker captures a valid Remote User Authentication Protocol interaction — including the enrolment in which Wallet Instance shares the AST.Authentication_Reference_Data Authentication Reference Data (ARD) with the WSCA-BE(TOE) — and brute forces the PIN by using the Wallet Instance to generate indefinite User Authentication Evidence (UAE) and verify it against the AST.Authentication_Reference_Data, without involvement of the WSCA-BE(TOE).                                                                                                 |
| T.WSCD_NET_ATTACK         | A network adversary performs active attacks (e.g. read, change, forge or reply) against the secure channel between the WSCD and the WSCA-BE. This includes compromising AST.WSCD_HSM_Access_Credentials.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| T.MULTI_TENANT            | An attacker manages to circumvent TOE user isolation mechanisms to gain unauthorized access to another users assets, using their AST.Attested_Key_Pairs and AST.WIA_Device_binding_Key_Pair.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| T.KEY_EXTRACT             | An attacker manages to abuse the WSCD-HSM client interface, using the AST.WSCD_HSM_Access_Credentials to extract HSM-stored private keys (e.g. AST.Attested_Key_Pairs, AST.WIA_Device_binding_Key_Pair and AST.WSCA_WSCD_ Signing_Key_Pair) from the WSCD_HSM.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| T.DERIVE                 | An attacker manages to derive any private key (AST.Attested_Key_Pairs, AST.WIA_Device_binding_Key_Pair, AST.WSCA_WSCD_Signing_Key_Pair), e.g. from key specific information like the public key or AST.Wrapped_Key_Blobs. |
| T.WSCA_USER_DATA_TAMPER  | An attacker manages to tamper with the S.WalletUser’s or S.WalletInstance’s AST.User_Data or AST.Wrapped_Key_Blobs to gain access to another S.WalletUser’s private keys.                                                 |
| T.PROVIDER_IMPERSONATION | An attacker forges or steals AST.Wallet_Provider_Authentication_Data in order to impersonate a Wallet Provider and get access to Wallet Provider specific functionality.                                                  |
| T.PROVIDER_NET_ATTACK    | An attacker forges or steals AST.Wallet_Provider_Authentication_Data in order to impersonate a Wallet Provider by attacking the mutual authenticated secure channel between the Wallet Provider and the WSCA.             |
| T.SIDE_CHANNEL           | A co-tenant on shared infrastructure components exploits side channels in the WSCA-BE’s processing of requests and responses to infer sensitive information about wallet user credentials.                                |
| T.AUDIT_TAMPER           | An attacker suppresses, modifies, deletes or causes incorrect attribution of security-relevant audit records, preventing detection or investigation of unauthorized WSCA-BE or WSCD-HSM operations.                       |

### 3.4 Organisational Security Policies {#s-3-4}

The organisational security policies (OSPs) as defined Table 4, shall apply to the WSCA-BE.

Table 4— Organisational Security Policies

| ID                    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| OSP.CRYPTO_STANDA RDS | The WSCA-BE shall use only cryptographic algorithms as mandated by the applicable implementing acts or as approved under the ECCG Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms (ACM) or equivalent successor documents, meeting minimum key length and algorithm selection requirements. Where a cryptographic mechanism required by the TOE is not yet included in the ECCG Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms, its use shall be subject to an appropriate security assessment and documented justification demonstrating that the mechanism provides sufficient security for the intended purpose and security strength. Such a mechanism shall only be used where its security has been established in accordance with the applicable certification or evaluation framework, and shall be replaced or updated when an applicable ECCG mechanism becomes available. |
| OSP.VULN_MGMT         | The TOE developer shall operate a vulnerability management process compliant with EN ISO/IEC 30111:2019 and the requirements of Article 5 of (EU) 2024/2981 or any of their successor documents.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| OSP.INFRA_SEC         | The server infrastructure hosting the WSCA-BE shall be operated under established policies and documented procedures that include physical access controls, privileged access management and change management processes appropriate for managing credentials at the eIDAS level of assurance high. Provider's conformity with these requirements are in-scope of the national certification scheme under TR 5.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| OSP.WSCD_CERT         | The WSCD-HSM shall be certified against an appropriate HSM Common Criteria Protection Profile. An appropriate Protection Profile is the CEN EN PP 419 221-5 or a different applicable Protection Profile providing at least equivalent functionality and assurance. Private keys stored in the HSM must be protected at least following the “assigned key” definition of the CEN EN PP 419 221-5.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| OSP.KEY_ISOLATION       | Each S.WalletUsers’s private keys shall be secured within the secure boundaries of the WSCD-HSM and bound to the S.WalletUsers’s identity in the WSCA-BE’s credential store. Key misuse shall not be possible without compromising the AST.WSCD_HSM_Access_Credentials or the WSCD-HSM itself.                                                                                                                                        |
| OSP.AUDIT               | The TOE shall maintain a cryptographically protected tamper-evident (non-repudiable) AST.Audit_Records of all security-relevant operations attributes to individual wallet user and transactions. The audit records shall be cryptographically integrity and authenticity protected. For each S.WalletInstance requested operation, the TOE shall generate evidence of origin and receipt that can be verified by a S.WalletProvider. |
| OSP.TOE_AUTHENTICA TION | The TOE shall be able to uniquely identify itself, its version and its configuration. Additionally, the TOE shall be able to authenticate itself to the user.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| OSP.SECURE_ERASURE      | Critical assets held by the WSCA-BE shall be securely erased on revocation, on deprovisioning, factory reset, and on an authorised deletion request.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| OSP.MIGRATION           | An authenticated Wallet User shall be allowed to migrate to a new wallet instance.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### 3.5 Assumptions {#s-3-5}

The assumptions, as defined in Table 5, describe the security properties of the operational environment. Security Targets shall provide evaluation evidence to confirm these assumptions are satisfied in the specific deployment.

Table 5— Assumptions

| ID                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| A.UAE_and_ARD          | It is assumed that the Wallet Instance cryptographically derives the User Authentication Evidence (UAE) from a knowledge-based factor (derived from the PIN) and a possession-based factor. A PUK is used to reset the knowledge-based factor in case the PIN was forgotten. It is assumed that User Authentication Evidence (UAE) and the Authentication Reference Data (ARD) preserve confidentiality and integrity of the knowledge-based factor (derived from the PIN) and a possession-based factor. Where part of the Wallet User authentication is verified outside the TOE, the external verification meets the requirements of CIR (EU) 2015/1502 Annex, sections 2.2.1 and 3.1, at level high. In particular the external mechanism provides dynamic authentication, protects against duplication and tampering by an attacker with high attack potential, and secures stored verification data against offline analysis. It is assumed that the Wallet Instance generate and uses the required cryptographic keys within the secure keystore. Additionally, the Wallet Instance app is assumed to be from an official app store and/or authenticated in a secure way. Additionally, the wallet shall only run on secure devices (including root/emulator detection, secure key storage capabilities, OS Version without related vulnerabilities) The wallet instance shall be certified according to (EU) 2024/2981. |
| A.PHYSICAL_PROTECT ION | The TOE is assumed to be physically protected in its operational environment and not subject to physical attacks that compromise the security. This protection is assumed to be sufficient to protect the TOE and the data it contains. As a result, the PP does not include any requirements on physical tamper protection or other physical attack mitigations (such as power analysis or EM analysis). The PP does not expect the product to defend against physical access to the TOE that allows unauthorized entities to extract data, bypass other controls, or otherwise manipulate the device.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| A.TRUSTED_ADMIN            | The Administrators are assumed to be trusted and to act in the best interest of security for the organization, following best practices for high trust environments. This includes appropriately trained, following policy, follow secure processes, and adhering to guidance documentation. Administrators are trusted to ensure passwords/credentials have sufficient strength and entropy and to lack malicious intent when administering the device. |
| A.TRUSTED_WALLET_ USER     | It is assumed that the S.WalletUser will not disclose their proof of knowledge.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| A.TRUSTED_WALLET_ PROVIDER | S.WalletProvider is assumed to be properly trained and trusted and will not disclose their AST.Wallet_Provider_Authentication_Data. S.WalletProvider is assumed to restrict admissible AST.Authentication_Reference_Data such that S.WalletUser can reliably protect their user authentication credentials.                                                                                                                                              |
| A.AUDIT_LOG_SERVER         | Audit log server is located in the TOE environment which is able to receive audit log messages from the TOE. The environment shall ensure that log data is not deleted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| A.DATABASE                 | External databases used for storage of TOE assets shall be located in the secure environment.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| A.GATEWAY                  | Internet facing gateways are excluded from the TOE scope and shall be used for, at least, DDoS protection, intrusion detection, antivirus functionality and firewall functionality.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

## 4 Security Objectives {#s-4}

### 4.1 Security Objectives for the TOE {#s-4-1}

The security objectives for the TOE are set out in Table 6.

Table 6 — TOE security objectives

| ID                 | Statement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| OT.KEY_PROTECT     | The WSCA-BE shall ensure that all private keys associated with wallet users are generated within and never exported from the secure boundaries of the WSCD-HSM. Only cryptographic algorithms as mandated by the applicable implementing acts or as approved under the ECCG Agreed Cryptographic Mechanisms (ACM) or equivalent successor documents, meeting minimum key length and algorithm selection requirements shall be used. The TOE itself shall only store a minimum set private and symmetric keys if necessary for basic TOE functionality, namely session keys and secure channel authentication data. The WSCA-BE shall hold only opaque key handles and shall enforce that all signing and key agreement operations are executed by the WSCD-HSM. The WSCA-BE shall protect at least AST.Authentication_Reference_Data, AST.Wallet_Instance_Authentication_Data and |
| OT.KEY_ISOLATION   | AST.Wallet_Provider_Authentication_Data. The WSCA-BE shall enforce per-wallet-unit key isolation by associating each key handle with the authenticated wallet user identity before invoking any WSCD-HSM operation. The WSCA-BE shall use the WSCA/WSCD signing key, only for signing the public key of key pairs generated within the WSCD- HSM and bind it to the wallet user. The WSCA-BE uses and protects per-key WSCD-HSM authorization credentials that only grant access to user keys connected to this credential. Per-key authorisation data is generated by the WSCD-HSM during key generation, then sent to the wallet instance and afterwards provided with each operation. The per-key authorization data is considered a TOE asset must be protected by the TOE during usage, and securely deleted when no longer needed by the TOE.                               |
| OT.SECURE_DELETION | Any TOE-stored assets shall be deleted in a secure manner. This includes a mechanism for secure factory reset.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| OT.USER_AUTH       | The WSCA-BE shall verify, before invoking any WSCD-HSM operation, that the request is accompanied by valid User Authentication Evidence (UAE) that is: (a) cryptographically bound to the specific wallet user’s registered Authentication Reference Data (ARD); (b) bound to the specific transaction context; (c) within its validity window; and (d) not previously used. (e) resilience against tampering or brute force attacks on the PIN (or PUK) verification. The WSCA-BE shall reject requests lacking valid evidence and record each rejection in the audit log.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| OT.PROVIDER_AUTH                  | The TOE shall mandate authentication of the S.WalletProvider before any provider related operation can be invoked.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| OT.API_CONTROL                    | The WSCA-BE shall ensure that authenticated S.WalletUser can only invoke operations on their own resources, unauthenticated requests are rejected before any sensitive processing. Each operation using keys must include the specific per-key authorization data to be provided by the S.WalletInstance.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| OT.WSCA_SECURE_CHANNEL            | The WSCA-BE(TOE) shall enforce a mutually authenticated secure channel between the TOE and the Wallet Instance. The WSCA-BE and the Wallets Instances will route all communication through the secure channel. The WSCA-BE(TOE) shall bind each transaction identifier to the AST.Wallet_Instance_Authentication_Data, preventing use of                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| OT.WSCD_SECURE_CHANNEL            | stolen User Authentication Evidence from a different client. The WSCA-BE(TOE) shall enforce a mutually authenticated secure channel between the TOE and the WSCD. The WSCA-BE and the WSCD will route all communication through the secure channel.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| OT.WALLET_PROVIDER_SECURE_CHANNEL | The WSCA-BE(TOE) shall enforce a mutually authenticated secure channel between the TOE and the Wallet Provider. The WSCA-BE and the Wallet Provider will route all communication through the secure channel.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| OT.MULTI_TENANT                   | The WSCA-BE shall implement strict isolation between wallet users such that an authenticated request from Wallet User A cannot access credentials, invoke WSCD-HSM operations using keys belonging to, or read records of Wallet User B.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| OT.AUDIT                          | The WSCA-BE shall generate a cryptographically protected tamper-evident audit record for each security-relevant event, including wallet user identifier; HSM key handle; relying party identifier (where applicable); User Authentication Evidence reference; and outcome and potential threats. Audit records shall be cryptographically integrity and authenticity protected. For each Wallet Instance requested operation, the TOE shall generate evidence of origin and receipt of the request so that can be verified by a Wallet Provider. Wallet Provider actions shall be logged. |
| OT.SELF_PROT                      | The WSCA-BE shall detect and refuse to start if its binary or configuration has been modified since the last integrity baseline. WSCD-HSM Access Credentials shall not be stored in plaintext within the WSCA-BE process or on storage.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| OT.PROTECTED_STORAGE              | The TOE shall protect the integrity and authenticity of all user data stored on the WSCA or its operative environment. This includes the key blobs, meta data, all user bindings and all authentication data stored outside of the WSCD. Additionally, all session keys and non-WSCD stored private keys shall be confidentiality protected. Any sensitive temporary data, including session keys and per-key authorization data, needs to be securely delete if not longer used.                                                                                                         |
| OT.AUTHENTICATION                 | The TOE is able to uniquely identify itself, its version and its configuration. Additionally, the TOE shall be able to authenticate itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

### 4.2 Security Objectives for the Operational Environment {#s-4-2}

The security objectives for the operational environment are set out in Table 7.

Table 7 — Operational environment security objectives

| ID                          | Statement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| OE.UAE_and_ARD              | The Wallet Instance will cryptographically bind the User Authentication Evidence (UAE) from a knowledge-based factor (derived from the PIN) and a possession-based factor. A PUK is used to reset the knowledge-based factor in case the PIN was forgotten. The Remote User Authentication Protocol (RUAP) implemented between User Authentication Evidence (UAE) and the Authentication Reference Data (ARD) will preserve confidentiality and integrity of the knowledge-based factor (derived from the PIN) and a possession-based factor (also when these are disclosed). Where part of the Wallet User authentication is verified outside the TOE, the external verification shall meet the requirements of CIR (EU) 2015/1502 Annex, sections 2.2.1 and 3.1, at level high. In particular the external mechanism provides dynamic authentication, protects against duplication and tampering by an attacker with high attack potential, and secures stored verification data against offline analysis. The Wallet Instance will generate and uses the required cryptographic keys within the secure keystore of the user device. |
| OE.RESISTANT_ARD            | The Wallet Provider restricts admissible ARD such that Wallet User can reliably protect their authentication credentials. ARD shall be constructed in way that knowledge-based factor cannot be verified without a secret held by the WSCA-BE or the WSCD.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| OE.HSM_CERT                 | The operational environment shall provide a WSCD-HSM certified against an appropriate HSM Common Criteria Protection Profile. An appropriate Protection Profile is the CEN EN PP 419 221-5 or a different applicable Protection Profile providing at least equivalent functionality and assurance. Private keys stored in the HSM must be protected at least following the 'assigned key' definition of the CEN EN PP 419 221-5.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| OE.INFRA_SEC                | The operational environment shall include physical and logical security controls for the WSCA-BE(TOE) infrastructure meeting OSP.INFRA_SEC, including privileged access management enforcing separation of duties, intrusion detection and change management. External databases (used for asset storage), gateways (used for at least DDoS protection) and the audit log server (OE.AUDIT_LOG_SERVER) shall be part of this secure operational environment. The operational environment needs to provide a reliable time source. The WSCA-BE(TOE) shall be operated on a hardened server using a least-privilege execution model.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| OE.ISOLATION                | The operational environment shall ensure that the WSCA-BE (TOE) process is isolated from other workloads, preventing memory access, network interception or storage tampering by co-hosted services.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| OE.PHYSICAL_PROTECTION      | The TOE is physically protected in its operational environment and not subject to physical attacks that compromise the security. The TOE underlying hardware is be hardened against remote side-channel attacks and microarchitectural attacks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| OE.VULNERABILITY_MANAGEMENT | The WSCA-BE developer operates a vulnerability management process compliant with EN ISO/IEC 30111:2019 or its successors and the requirements of Article 5 of (EU) 2024/2981.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| OE.GENUINE_WALLET_INSTANCE | The Wallet Instance app is sourced to be from an official app store and/or authenticated in a secure way. Additionally, the wallet shall only run on secure devices (including root/emulator detection, secure key storage capabilities, OS Version without related vulnerabilities) The wallet instance shall be certified according to (EU) 2024/2981. Each Wallet user has exactly one Wallet Instance.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| OE.SECURE_UPDATE           | The wallet provider shall ensure that WSCA-BE(TOE) software updates are cryptographically signed, that the deployment pipeline verifies signatures before installation and that a SBOM is maintained for each deployed version.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| OE.TRUSTED_ADMIN           | The Administrators are trusted and to act in the best interest of security for the organization, following best practices for high trust environments. This includes appropriately trained, following policy, and adhering to guidance documentation. Administrators are trusted to ensure passwords/credentials have sufficient strength and entropy and to lack malicious intent when administering the device. The TOE is not expected to be capable of defending against a malicious Administrator that actively works to bypass or compromise the security.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| OE.TRUSTED_WALLET_USER     | The Wallet User will not share or disclose their knowledge or possession authentication factors with 3 rd parties.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| OE.TRUSTED_WALLET_PROVIDER | All Wallet Provider personnel shall be properly trained and trusted, and shall not disclose the TOE-related authentication data. The Wallet Provider shall protect the public part of AST.WSCA_WSCD_Signing_Key_Pair, and the complete signing key chain used to issue the Key Attestation and the Wallet Instance Attestation, against unauthorised disclosure, modification and substitution. The Wallet Provider shall verify the authenticity of attested public keys received from the WSCA-BE before including them in a Key Attestation or a Wallet Instance Attestation. The Wallet Provider shall preserve the confidentiality and integrity of the Key Attestation and the Wallet Instance Attestation throughout the attestation process. The Wallet Provider shall ensure that any process by which a Wallet User assets are migrated, it requires identity re-verification at an assurance level equivalent to the assurance level of the Wallet Unit before the reset or migration is permitted. |
| OE.AUDIT_LOG_SERVER        | Audit log server is located in the secure TOE environment as described in OE.INFRA_SEC which is able to receive audit log messages from the TOE. The environment shall ensure that log data is not deleted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

## 5 Extended components definition {#s-5}

### 5.1 Protected Audit Event Storage (FAU\_STG\_EXT) {#s-5-1}

## Family Behaviour

This component defines the requirements for the TSF to be able to securely transmit audit data between the TOE and an external IT entity. This is a new family defined for the FAU class.

Note: FAU\_STG\_EXT is inspired by ‘collaborative Protection Profile for Network Devices’, version 4.0, 2025-11-25.

## Component Levelling

![Image](/img/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/nl-cs-wsca/image_000002_f384b2913c77491b6e7743136333119a9c5252c8591207240c3210925db74390.png)

| FAU_STG_EXT.1   | Protected audit event storage requires the TSF to use a trusted channel implementing a secure protocol.                                            |
|-----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| FAU_STG_EXT.2   | Counting lost audit data requires the TSF to provide information about audit records affected when the audit log becomes full.                     |
| FAU_STG_EXT.3   | Notification in Case of Possible Audit Data Loss requires the TSF to generate a warning before the audit trail exceeds the local storage capacity. |

## Management: FAU\_STG\_EXT.1, FAU\_STG\_EXT.2, FAU\_STG\_EXT.3

The following actions could be considered for the management functions in FMT:

- a) There are no management functions foreseen.

## Audit: FAU\_STG\_EXT.1, FAU\_STG\_EXT.2, FAU\_STG\_EXT.3

The following actions should be auditable for FAU\_GEN Security audit data generation and if FAU\_GEN\_EXT is included in the PP/ST:

- a) There are no auditable events foreseen.

#### 5.1.1 FAU\_STG\_EXT.1 Protected Audit Event Storage {#s-5-1-1}

| FAU_STG_EXT.1    | Protected Audit Event Storage                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Hierarchical to: | No other components.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Dependencies:    | FAU_GEN.1 Audit data generation FAU_COP.1 Cryptographic operation                                                                                                                                                   |
| FAU_STG_EXT.1.1  | The TSF shall be able to transmit the generated audit data to an external IT entity.                                                                                                                                |
| FAU_STG_EXT.1.2  | The TSF shall be able to store generated audit data on the TOE itself.                                                                                                                                              |
| FAU_STG_EXT.1.3  | The TSF shall maintain a [selection: log file, database, buffer, [assignment: other local logging method]] of audit records in the event that an interruption of communication with the remote audit server occurs. |

| FAU_STG_EXT.1.4   | The TSF shall be able to store [selection: persistent, non-persistent] audit records locally with a minimum storage size of [assignment: number of records and/or file/buffer size(s)].   |
|-------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### 5.2 Authentication protocol with transaction binding FIA\_UAE\_EXT {#s-5-2}

## Family Behaviour

The following extended SFR family FIA\_UAE\_EXT is defined to address the specific security requirement for remote, transaction-bound user authentication evidence. This is a new family defined for the FIA class.

## Component Levelling

FIA\_UAE\_EXT Authentication protocol with transaction binding

FIA\_UAE\_EXT.1

1

2

Requires the TSF to issue a challenge, bind it to a transaction context, and verify returned evidence against the user's authentication reference data before performing a controlled operation.

FIA\_UAE\_EXT.2

Records issued challenges and accepted evidence, and to deny operations where the evidence relies on an unknown, already consumed or expired challenge.

## Management: FIA\_UAE\_EXT.1, FIA\_UAE\_EXT.2

The following actions could be considered for the management functions in FMT:

- a) There are no management functions foreseen.

## Audit: FIA\_UAE\_EXT.1, FIA\_UAE\_EXT.2

The following actions should be auditable for FAU\_GEN Security audit data generation:

- a) Minimal: Failure of verification of authentication evidence
- b) Basic: success and failure of verification of authentication evidence, and the reason for failure

#### 5.2.1 FIA\_UAE\_EXT.1 Transaction-bound authentication evidence {#s-5-2-1}

| FIA_UAE _EXT.1   | Transaction-bound authentication evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Hierarchical to: | No other components.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Dependencies:    | FIA_UID.1 Timing of identification FIA_ATD.1 User attribute definition [FCS_RBG.1 Random bit generation or FCS_RNG.1 Generation of random] FCS_COP.1 Cryptographic operation FPT_STM.1 Reliable time stamps                                                                                                    |
| FIA_UAE_EXT.1.1  | The TSF shall generate, for each request to perform an operation in [assignment: list of operations requiring authentication evidence], a challenge with a minimum of [assignment: number of bits] of entropy obtained from a random bit generation function meeting [selection: FCS_RBG.1, FCS_RNG.1].        |
| FIA_UAE_EXT.1.2  | The TSF shall construct, for each challenge, a transaction context comprising the challenge, the identity of the user, the requested operation, and [assignment: other transaction attributes], and shall associate that transaction context with the communication session on which the request was received. |
| FIA_UAE_EXT.1.3  | The TSF shall require that authentication evidence cryptographically bound to the transaction context of the requested operation be presented before the TSF performs any operation in [assignment: list of operations requiring authentication evidence].                                                     |
| FIA_UAE_EXT.1.4  | The TSF shall verify presented authentication evidence against the authentication reference data associated with the identified user and shall verify that the evidence demonstrates that each authentication factor in [assignment: list of authentication factors] was verified.                             |
| FIA_UAE_EXT.1.5  | The TSF shall verify that presented authentication evidence was received no more than [assignment: validity period] after the corresponding challenge was issued.                                                                                                                                              |
| FIA_UAE_EXT.1.6  | The TSF shall deny the requested operation if any verification required by FIA_UAE_EXT.1.3, FIA_UAE_EXT.1.4 or FIA_UAE_EXT.1.5 fails.                                                                                                                                                                          |

#### 5.2.2 FIA\_UAE\_EXT.2 Single-use enforcement for authentication evidence {#s-5-2-2}

| FIA_UAE _EXT.2   | Single-use enforcement for authentication evidence                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Hierarchical to: | No other components.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Dependencies:    | FIA_UAE_EXT.1 Transaction-bound authentication evidence FPT_STM.1 Reliable time stamps                                                                                                                                                 |
| FIA_UAE_EXT.2.1  | The TSF shall maintain a nonce registry covering all transaction identifiers issued and all evidence received within the validity window defined in FIA_UAE_EXT.1.5.                                                                   |
| FIA_UAE_EXT.2.2  | The TSF shall deny the requested operation if the presented authentication evidence refers to a challenge that was not issued by the TSF, that has already been used in successful verification, or whose validity period has expired. |

## 6 Security Functional Requirements {#s-6}

All SFRs are drawn from CC Part 2 unless identified as extended components. Operations are marked as following:

- Assignment (A): indicated with text in italic. If assignments are possible options for the ST author, it is marked as [assignment: XYZ];
- Refinement (R): indicated with text in bold, and strikethrough;
- Selection (S): selection values adopted in the PP is underlined. If selections are possible options for the ST author, it is marked as [selection: XYZ];
- Iteration (I): indicated by adding a string starting with ‘/’ (e.g. ‘FCS\_COP.1/Hash’)

FAU\_STG\_EXT.3.1

## Application Note 1

The technical administrator is not a user role for the TOE itself. This administrator is responsible for the maintenance of the operative environment, including the underlying server

### 6.2 Class FCO — Communication {#s-6-2}

#### 6.2.1 FCO\_NRO.2 Enforced proof of origin {#s-6-2-1}

| FCO_NRO.2.1   | The TSF shall enforce the generation of evidence of origin for transmitted API requests from the Wallet Instance handled by the TOE at all times.                                                    |
|---------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| FCO_NRO.2.2   | The TSF shall be able to relate the Wallet Instance identifier of the originator of the information, and the transaction identifier, UTC timestamp of the information to which the evidence applies. |
| FCO_NRO.2.3   | The TSF shall provide a capability to verify the evidence of origin of information to the Wallet Provider given the corresponding audit record is retained by the audit log server.                  |

## Application Note 2

The TSF shall enforce generation of evidence of origin for all signing operations. The evidence shall be a digital signature computed by the WSCD-HSM over the hash submitted by the Wallet Instance. The audit record shall bind the wallet instance identifier, the transaction identifier, and the UTC timestamp to the signing event, providing nonrepudiation of the signing operation.

#### 6.2.2 FCO\_NRR.2 Enforced proof of receipt {#s-6-2-2}

| FCO_NRR.2.1   | The TSF shall enforce the generation of evidence of receipt for received API requests from the Wallet Instance handled by the TOE at all times.                                                                                              |
|---------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| FCO_NRR.2.2   | The TSF shall be able to relate the session identifier of the recipient of the information, and the Wallet Instance’s certificate, public key or thumbprint and the transaction identifier of the information to which the evidence applies. |

FCO\_NRR.2.3

The TSF shall provide a capability to verify the evidence of receipt of information to the Wallet Provider given the corresponding audit record is retained by the audit log server.

## Application Note 3

The TSF shall record evidence of receipt of each signing request, including the session identifier, the Wallet Instance’s certificate, public key or thumbprint and the transaction identifier.

|---------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

## Application Note 8

The TSF shall either use the WSCD-HSM’s certified DRBG or the server OS’s CSPRNG (seeded from hardware entropy) for generation of random numbers. In case the HSM DRBG is used, the HSM certification shall be referenced. Otherwise, this SFR needs to be claimed by the ST author (in this case the ST author shall additionally add FCS\_DRB.2 or FCS\_DRB.3, depending in the implementation of the actual TOE). Additionally, the ST author shall cover the DRBG in FPT\_TST.1 and FPT\_FLS.1.

FDP\_ACC.1.1/Key\_

Creation The TSF shall enforce the Key Creation SFP on

#### 6.4.5 FDP\_ACC.1/Operation Access Control Policy {#s-6-4-5}

The TSF shall enforce the Operation SFP on

FDP\_ACC.1.1/Operation

- Subject: Wallet User
- Objects: Wallet User user-bound assets (including keys or key pairs)
- Operations: (Per-key-authorized) Operations with Wallet User user-bound assets

The TOE instructs the WSCD to carry out operations on and with the Wallet Users assets only where it corresponds to an assets within the WSCD-HSM that is bound to the identified Wallet User using per-key-authorization data provided by the wallet instance.

- Subject: Wallet User
- Objects: Wallet User user-bound assets (including keys or key pairs)
- Operations: PIN reset

The TOE instructs the WSCD to carry out PIN reset when the correct PUK was provided.

- Subject: Wallet User
- Objects: Wallet User user bound assets
- Operation: Wallet User can clear or delete the Wallet User bound assets or migrate them to a different Wallet Instance. (This does not include the WSCD-stored plaintext private keys, only their reference, keyblobs and management).

#### 6.5.4 FIA\_ATD.1/Wallet User attribute definition {#s-6-5-4}

The TSF shall maintain the following list of security attributes belonging to individual users:

- a) wallet instance and wallet user identifier
- b) the registered Wallet Instance authentication credential, used both for authentication of the communication session and for verification of signatures over User Authentication Evidence
- c) the Authentication Reference Data against which the knowledge- and possessionbased factor of the User Authentication Evidence is verified
- d) the binding records associating the wallet user with its wrapped key blobs, its attested key pairs and, where the WIA device-binding key pair is managed by the WSCA/WSCD, that key pair
- e) the per-key authorisation data associated with the wallet user for access to the WSCD-HSM, for the duration of the operation for which it was provided
- f) the authentication failure counter
- g) the wallet user status (active / suspended / deprovisioned)
- h) the integrity check value and version counter bound to the stored attributes of the wallet user
- i) [assignment: additional user security attributes].

FIA\_ATD.1.1/Wallet

#### 6.5.5 FIA\_ATD.1/Provider User attribute definition {#s-6-5-5}

The TSF shall maintain the following list of security attributes belonging to individual users:

- a) the Wallet Provider identifier
- b) the Wallet Provider authentication reference data
- c) [assignment: additional provider security attributes]

FIA\_ATD.1.1/Provider

- the binding records in FIA\_ATD.1.1/Wallet
- the per-key authorisation data in FIA\_ATD.1.1/Wallet
- [assignment: list of user security attributes]

### 6.6 Class FMT — Security Management {#s-6-6}

#### 6.6.1 FMT\_SMR.1 Security roles {#s-6-6-1}

FMT\_SMR.1.1

The TSF shall maintain the roles

- Wallet User
- Wallet Instance
- Wallet Provider
- [assignment: additional authorized identified roles].

#### 6.6.2 FMT\_SMF.1 Specification of Management Functions {#s-6-6-2}

The TSF shall be capable of performing the following management functions:

- For the Wallet Provider:
    - TOE unique self-identification of version and configuration
    - TOE maintenance
    - Audit data review
    - Factory Reset
    - Deletion or reset of user authentication data
    - [assignment: list of management functions to be provided by the TSF].
- For the Wallet User:
    - Modifying user authentication data
    - PIN reset using PUK
    - Wallet Instance Migration

FMT\_SMF.1.1

#### 6.6.3 FMT\_MSA.1/User\_Creation Management of security attributes {#s-6-6-3}

FMT\_MSA.1.1/ User\_Creation The TSF shall enforce the User Creation SFP to restrict the ability to modify the security attributes that are Wallet User related as defined in FIA\_USB.1/Wallet to the Wallet Provider or Wallet Instance.

#### 6.6.4 FMT\_MSA.3/User\_Creation Static attribute initialization {#s-6-6-4}

FMT\_MSA.3.1/ User\_Creation

FMT\_MSA.3.2/ User\_Creation The TSF shall enforce the User Creation SFP to provide restrictive default values for security attributes that are used to enforce the SFP.

The TSF shall allow the Wallet Provider or Wallet Instance to specify alternative initial values to override the default values when an object or information is created.

#### 6.6.5 FMT\_MSA.1/Key\_Management Management of security attributes {#s-6-6-5}

FMT\_MSA.1.1/ Key\_Management The TSF shall enforce the Key Management SFP to restrict the ability to modify, delete the security attributes Wallet User keys related attributes as defined in FIA\_USB.1/Wallet to the Wallet Instance or Wallet Provider (deletion only).

#### 6.6.6 FMT\_MSA.3/Key\_Management Static attribute initialization {#s-6-6-6}

FMT\_MSA.3.1/ Key\_Management The TSF shall enforce the Key Management SFP to provide restrictive default values for security attributes that are used to enforce the SFP.

FMT\_MSA.3.2/ Key\_Management The TSF shall allow the Wallet Instance to specify alternative initial values to override the default values when an object or information is created.

#### 6.6.7 FMT\_MSA.1/Operation Management of security attributes {#s-6-6-7}

FMT\_MSA.1.1/ Operation The TSF shall enforce the Operation SFP to restrict the ability to query the security attributes Wallet User keys related attributes as defined in FIA\_USB.1/Wallet to the Wallet User.

#### 6.6.8 FMT\_MSA.2 Secure security attributes {#s-6-6-8}

FMT\_MSA.2.1

The TSF shall ensure that only secure values are accepted for attributes defined in FIA\_USB.1/Wallet and FIA\_USB.1/Provider.

#### 6.6.9 FMT\_MTD.1/Provider Management of TSF data {#s-6-6-9}

FMT\_MTD.1.1/Provider The TSF shall restrict the ability to modify the Wallet Provider and WSCD authentication data to Wallet Provider.

#### 6.6.10 FMT\_MTD.1/User Management of TSF data {#s-6-6-10}

FMT\_MTD.1.1/Provider The TSF shall restrict the ability to modify the their Wallet User authentication data to an authenticated Wallet User. However, delete and clear are available for the Wallet Provider.

#### 6.6.11 FMT\_MTD.1/Instance Management of TSF data {#s-6-6-11}

FMT\_MTD.1.1/Provider The TSF shall restrict the ability to modify the their Wallet Instance authentication data to an authenticated Wallet Instance. However, delete and clear are available for the Wallet Provider.

### 6.7 Class FPT — Protection of the TSF {#s-6-7}

#### 6.7.1 FPT\_FLS.1 Failure with preservation of secure state {#s-6-7-1}

FPT\_FLS.1.1

The TSF shall preserve a secure state when the following types of failures occur: WSCDHSM connection failure; credential store integrity check failure; audit log unavailability; [assignment: additional types of failures in the TSF].

#### 6.7.2 FPT\_ITC.1 Inter-TSF confidentiality during transmission {#s-6-7-2}

FPT\_ITC.1.1

The TSF shall protect all TSF data transmitted from the TSF to another trusted IT product the WSCD-HSM from unauthorized disclosure during transmission.

## Application Note 10

This is applicable for channel with the WSCD-HSM.

#### 6.7.3 FPT\_ITI.1 Inter-TSF detection of modification {#s-6-7-3}

| FPT_ITI.1.1   | The TSF shall provide the capability to detect modification of all TSF data during transmission between the TSF and another trusted IT product the WSCD-HSM within the following metric: [assignment: a defined modification metric].   |

#### 6.7.4 FPT\_RCV.4 Function recovery {#s-6-7-4}

FPT\_RCV.4.1

The TSF shall ensure that all credential management and HSM operations [assignment: additional list of functions and failure scenarios] have the property that the function either completes successfully, or for the indicated failure scenarios, recovers to a consistent and secure state.

## Application Note 12

The TSF shall ensure that all credential management and HSM operations are transactional: either they complete fully — including HSM confirmation and audit record creation — or they are rolled back to the prior state, with an audit record of the failure.

## Application Note 13

The TSF shall maintain a mutually authenticated, encrypted channel to the WSCD-HSM providing: identification of the HSM via its hardware attestation certificate; protection against replay of HSM commands using per-command sequence numbers or nonces; and detection of any modification or substitution of HSM responses. The TSF shall refuse to use HSM responses that fail integrity verification.

## 7 Security Assurance Requirements {#s-7}

The assurance package is EAL4 augmented with AVA\_VAN.5, ALC\_DVS.2 and ALC\_FLR.3. The required assurance components and their architecture-specific evaluation focus are defined in Table 8.

Table 8 — Security assurance requirements

|-------------|--------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ADV_ARC.1   | Security Architecture Description    | Shall document the WSCA-BE’s multi-tenant isolation model, the RAC protocol and the HSM client interface.                                                                                     |
| ADV_FSP.4   | Complete Functional Specification    | Shall cover the RAC API endpoint, all HSM command types invoked, all credential store operations and all internal inter-module interfaces.                                                    |
| ADV_IMP.1   | Implementation Representation        | Source code of the WSCA-BE, including the RAC handler, HSM client library, credential store and audit subsystem.                                                                              |
| ADV_TDS.3   | Basic Modular Design                 | Module-level design showing: RAC authentication module; FCS_EXT_UAE evidence verification module; access control engine; HSM client module; credential store; audit module; nonce registry.   |
| AGD_OPE.1   | Operational User Guidance            | Shall include: HSM configuration and partition setup; WSCA-BE deployment guide; privileged access management requirements; incident response procedures.                                      |
| AGD_PRE.1   | Preparative Procedures               | Secure installation and configuration procedures, including HSM initialisation, credential store and integrity baseline creation.                                                             |
| ALC_CMC.4   | Production Support and CM Automation | Configuration management system with automated acceptance procedures and production support.                                                                                                  |
| ALC_CMS.4   | Problem Tracking CM Coverage         | CM coverage for all TOE elements including problem reports and security vulnerabilities.                                                                                                      |
