| ALC_LCD.1   | Developer Defined Life- Cycle Model  | A documented life-cycle model used in development and maintenance of the WSCA-BE.                                                                                                             |
| ALC_TAT.1   | Well-Defined Development Tools       | Documented development tools, compiler options and build configurations.                                                                                                                      |
| ASE_CCL.1   | Conformance Claims                   | ST conformance claim to this PP.                                                                                                                                                              |
| ASE_ECD.1   | Extended Components Definition       | Full definition of the FCS_EXT_UAE.1 and FCS_EXT_UAE.2 extended component family, including component hierarchy, management and audit requirements.                                           |

| ATE_COV.2   | Analysis of Coverage                       | Shall demonstrate test coverage of all RAC endpoints, all FCS_EXT_UAE evidence verification paths (positive and negative), all multi-tenant isolation boundaries and all HSM error handling paths.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

## 8 Requirement Objective and Dependency Rationale {#s-8}

### 8.1 Security Objectives Rationale {#s-8-1}

Table 9 traces each Threat, OSP and Assumption to the security objectives that address it and provides the rationale for the coverage.

Table 9 — Objectives traceability

| Threat / OSP / Assumption   | Maps to objective(s)                                                                                                                | Rationale TOE updates are signed and verified                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| T.WSCA_FW_TAMPER            | OE.SECURE_UPDATE OE.VULNERABILITY_MANAGEMENT OE.INFRA_SEC OE.TRUSTED_ADMIN OE.HSM_CERT OT.SELF_PROT OT.KEY_PROTECT OT.KEY_ISOLATION | before installation, with an SBOM for each deployed version (OE.SECURE_UPDATE). Compromise of the hosting environment is addressed by change management and intrusion detection (OE.INFRA_SEC). The WSCD- HSM is a certified product (OE.HSM_CERT). Software vulnerability: the developer identifies and remediates vulnerabilities (OE.VULNERABILITY_MANAGEMENT), fixes are delivered through the signed update path (OE.SECURE_UPDATE), a modified binary or configuration is detected at start-up (OT.SELF_PROT), and the least-privilege execution model limits what an exploited process can reach (OE.INFRA_SEC). Insider threat: privileged access management for infrastructure administrators with separation of duties (OE.INFRA_SEC), and trusted administrators, with the residual risk of a malicious administrator stated explicitly (OE.TRUSTED_ADMIN). If the TOE is compromised, its own checks cannot be relied on, and protection rests on controls that do not depend on it: no private key material exists in the TOE (OT.KEY_PROTECT), the WSCD-HSM protects keys as assigned keys usable only with their own authorisation data (OE.HSM_CERT), and that authorisation data is held per key (OT.KEY_ISOLATION). A compromised TOE therefore cannot extract keys, and can use a key only while it holds that key's authorisation data. |

The WSCD-HSM is reached by the TOE over a trusted channel (FTP_ITC.1/WSCD-HSM). FDP_ACF.1.4/Operation denies any direct key access or key export request for keys residing in the WSCD, so the TOE holds no unencrypted key material. The Key Management SFP restricts who may create or delete keys, and FMT_MSA.1/Key_Management, FMT_MSA.1/Operation and FMT_MSA.3/Key_Management restrict and initialise the associated attributes. The FCS components cover only operations the TOE performs itself, supported by FMT_MSA.2. Operations performed by the WSCD are referred to the WSCD ST. All cryptographic mechanisms follow OSP.CRYPTO_STANDARDS. |

| OT.SECURE_DELETION | FCS_CKM.6 FDP_ACC.1/Key_Management FDP_ACF.1/Key_Management FMT_SMF.1 FDP_RIP.2                                         | FCS_CKM.6.1 requires destruction of all TSF generated and maintained keys and key material on revocation, deprovisioning, factory reset and authorised deletion. The Key Management SFP (FDP_ACC.1/Key_Management and FDP_ACF.1/Key_Management) restricts who may request deletion, FMT_SMF.1 provides factory reset as a management function, and FDP_RIP.2 ensures that residual content is unavailable on deallocation.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

FIA_USB.1.2/Wallet prevents the attributes of one wallet user being associated with a subject acting for another and prevents association where the status is other than active or where an integrity error has been detected. FMT_MSA.1 and FMT_MSA.3 restrict and initialise the attributes on which those decisions depend. |

FAU_STG_EXT.1.6 requires the authenticity and integrity of audit data to be ensured by cryptographic means, whether held on the TOE or on an external entity, which is the tamper-evidence the objective demands; FAU_STG_EXT.1.1 to .1.5 govern transmission and local retention, FAU_STG_EXT.2 counts losses and FAU_STG_EXT.3 warns before capacity is exceeded. FCO_NRO.2 and FCO_NRR.2 add evidence of origin and receipt verifiable by the Wallet Provider, and FAU_SAR.1 gives the Wallet Provider the means to read the records.                                                                                                                                             |
| OT.SELF_PROT | FPT_INI.1 FPT_TST.1 FPT_FLS.1 FPT_RCV.4 FDP_RIP.2 FDP_SDC.1                                 | FPT_INI.1 provides a self-protected initialisation function that verifies the integrity of the software binary and configuration and halts on failure. FPT_TST.1 runs self-tests at start-up and periodically over the cryptographic libraries, the WSCD-HSM connection, the credential store and the transaction identifier registry. FPT_FLS.1 preserves a secure state on the named failures and FPT_RCV.4 makes credential management and HSM operations transactional. FDP_RIP.2 prevents recovery of residual content. FDP_SDC.1 ensures the confidentiality of the WSCD-HSM access credentials wherever they are stored, and FDP_RIP.2 ensures that the plaintext copy used in process memory to authenticate to the WSCD-HSM is made unavailable when that memory is deallocated. |

FDP_ACF.1.2/Operation requires the integrity of all operation-related assets to be verified before an operation proceeds. The HSM provides the cryptographic operation used to compute and verify the check values and to protect stored data in confidence. FMT_MTD.1/Instance and FMT_MTD.1/User protect user authentication data from unauthorized modification. FDP_RIP.2 mandates the secure removal of deallocated assets, including potential session keys and per-key authentication data. |

Self- Authentication is part of the mutually secure channel FTP_PRO.*.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

### 8.4 Security Assurance Requirements Rationale {#s-8-4}

EAL4 augmented with ALC\_DVS.2, ALC\_FLR.3 and AVA\_VAN.5 is required for this type of product since it is intended to withstand sophisticated attacks.

ALC\_DVS.2 covers physical, procedural and personal procedures in place in the development environment. This prevents leakage of design and implementation details that would make attacks easier. ALC\_DVS.2 replaces ALC\_DVS.1 which is part of the EAL4 package.

ALC\_FLR.3 covers flaw remediation handling and does not have any dependencies by itself and can therefore be easily augmented to EAL4.

AVA\_VAN.5 is augmented as the TOE shall be highly resistant to any kind of penetration attacks; its dependencies are already fulfilled by EAL4.

| R10 — Transaction manipulation      | T.WSCA_NET_ATTACK; T.WSCD_NET_ATTACK; T.WSCA_ATTESTATION_TAMPER; T.WSCA_DATA_TAMPER. Assets: AST.Channel_Authentication_Session_Key, AST.Attested_Key_Pairs, AST.User_Data. | Addresses manipulation of communications, attestation inputs and TOE data. Binding cryptographic operations to the complete transaction context is not explicitly established by the current SPD and requires additional wallet-system controls.              |
| R11 — Repudiation                   | T.AUDIT_TAMPER. Asset: AST.Audit_Records. OSP.AUDIT.                                                                                                                        | Directly addresses suppression, modification, deletion and incorrect attribution of security-relevant audit records. OSP.AUDIT requires tamper-evident records and evidence of operation origin and receipt.                                                 |
| R12 — Transaction data disclosure   | T.WSCA_NET_ATTACK; T.WSCD_NET_ATTACK; T.SIDE_CHANNEL; T.WALLET_ORACLE. Assets: AST.Channel_Authentication_Session_Key, AST.Authentication_Reference_Data, AST.User_Data.    | Addresses disclosure of sensitive information through communications, side channels and authentication-related attacks. Explicit classification and minimisation of transaction data would strengthen coverage.                                               |
| R13 — Service disruption            | T.WSCA_DATA_TAMPER; T.WSCA_NET_ATTACK; T.WSCD_NET_ATTACK.                                                                                                                   | Addresses attacks that could compromise service operation or availability. The current threats do not explicitly cover denial of service, resource exhaustion, component failure or recovery and requires additional wallet-system controls.                 |
| R14 — Surveillance                  | T.SIDE_CHANNEL; T.WSCA_NET_ATTACK. Assets: AST.User_Data, AST.Audit_Records.                                                                                                | Addresses potential leakage of sensitive information through side channels and network observation. Protection against systematic correlation or tracking of users and transactions is not explicitly covered and requires additional wallet-system controls. |

## B (informative) Completeness Analysis of the Security Problem Definition {#s-b}

This appendix provides a completeness analysis of the Security Problem Definition (SPD) of the WSCA-BE Protection Profile in Chapter 3.

The purpose of the analysis is to demonstrate that the identified assets, subjects, threats, Organisational Security Policies (OSPs), and assumptions provide sufficient coverage of the security concerns arising from the defined TOE scope, its security functionality, and its operational environment.

The analysis is based on the TOE definition and security functionality described in this Protection Profile. In particular, the analysis considers the WSCA-BE security functions, the assets managed or protected by the TOE, the interactions with the Wallet Instance, Wallet Provider and WSCD-HSM, and the environmental dependencies defined for the TOE.

A security concern is considered covered when it is represented by at least one of the following:

- a Threat, where an adverse action by a threat agent must be prevented or detected;
- an Organisational Security Policy, where a security requirement is imposed on the TOE or its operation by an applicable policy or regulation; or
- an Assumption, where the security property is provided by the operational environment or by another component outside the TOE boundary.

### B.1 Coverage of the TOE Security Functionality {#s-b-1}

The TOE overview, in section 1.2, identifies the WSCA-BE as a security-critical backend component responsible for, among other functions, authentication and authorisation, key lifecycle management, protected cryptographic operations, attestation support, multi-tenant isolation, security audit and self-protection. These functions form the basis for the completeness analysis.

The analysis shows that each principal security function identified in the TOE description is represented in the SPD by one or more threats, OSPs or environmental assumptions.

### B.3 Coverage of the Operational Environment {#s-b-3}

The WSCA-BE (TOE) operates as part of the Wallet ecosystem and relies on a number of external entities and supporting components that are outside the TOE boundary. The TOE introduction identifies the Wallet Instance, User Device, Wallet Provider Backend, Wallet User, Wallet Provider, WSCD-HSM, PID/Attestation Providers, Relying Parties, Access Certificate Infrastructure, gateway servers, external database and external log server as components or entities interacting with or supporting the TOE.

Table 15 verifies that the security dependencies on these external entities are explicitly represented in the Security Problem Definition. For each external entity or component, the analysis identifies the corresponding Assumption and/or Organisational Security Policy that establishes the security conditions on which the TOE relies.

Table 15 — Coverage of the Operational Environment

| External entity / component                              | Security dependency of the TOE                                                                                                                                                                            | Assumption / OSP                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|----------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Wallet Instance (WI)                                     | The Wallet Instance must securely generate and protect authentication evidence, establish the required secure communication, use secure key storage, and correctly mediate User interaction with the TOE. | A.UAE_and_ARD                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Wallet User                                              | The User must protect the knowledge-based authentication factor and must not disclose authentication secrets.                                                                                             | A.TRUSTED_WALLET_USER                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Wallet Provider Backend (WPB)                            | The Wallet Provider must use authenticated communication, protect its authentication data, correctly manage Wallet Units and provide valid authorization requests to the TOE.                             | A.TRUSTED_WALLET_PROVIDER                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Wallet Provider                                          | The Wallet Provider is trusted to protect its authentication data and to operate the Wallet Provider functionality according to the required security procedures.                                         | A.TRUSTED_WALLET_PROVIDER                                                                                                                                                                         |
| WSCD-HSM                                                 | The WSCD-HSM must protect private keys, prevent unauthorized export or use of protected keys, and provide the required secure cryptographic functionality.                                                | OSP.WSCD_CERT, OSP.KEY_ISOLATION                                                                                                                                                                  |
| WSCD-HSM operational environment                         | The physical and operational environment of the WSCD-HSM must prevent unauthorized physical compromise.                                                                                                   | A.PHYSICAL_PROTECTION                                                                                                                                                                             |
| PID/Attestation Providers                                | Providers must correctly authenticate the Wallet Unit, validate WIA/KA information and proof-of-possession, and use the applicable trust infrastructure when issuing credentials.                        | PID/Attestation Providers are only indirectly connected to the TOE via the Wallet Instance. No assumptions on PID/Attestation Providers are expected in this protection profile for the WSCA-BE.  |
| Relying Parties (RP)                                     | Relying Parties must authenticate using the applicable certificates, correctly verify presentations and use the disclosed information according to the applicable requirements.                           | Relying parties are only indirectly connected to the TOE via the Wallet Instance. No assumptions on relying parties are expected in this protection profile for the WSCA-BE.                      |
| Access Certificate Infrastructure / Trust Infrastructure | The trust infrastructure must provide trustworthy trust anchors and certificate information used by ecosystem entities to authenticate one another.                                                       | Keys in the WSCA/WSCD are not part of the Access Certificate Infrastructure / Trust Infrastructure. No assumptions on this infrastruture are expected in this protection profile for the WSCA-BE. |
| Gateway / Internet-facing gateway                       | The gateway must protect the TOE from external network attacks and provide the specified network security functions.                                                                                      | A.GATEWAY                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| External Database                                        | The database storing TOE assets must be located in the secure environment and must provide the required protection for TOE-managed data.                                                                  | A.DATABASE                                                                                                                                                                                        |

| Server / hosting infrastructure | The infrastructure hosting the TOE must provide physical protection, controlled privileged access and secure administration. | A.PHYSICAL_PROTECTION, A.TRUSTED_ADMIN, OSP.INFRA_SEC |
| TOE administrators              | Administrators must be trusted, appropriately trained and follow the defined secure administration procedures.               | A.TRUSTED_ADMIN                                       |

Therefore, operational environment is considered complete with respect to the external entities and components identified in the TOE architecture.
